commitResults.messageTitle: Updated AGENTS.md with user setup details
Level-0: renamed chatbot to Echo, added greeting and exit, and updated Java setup instructions.

Level-1: Updated the code to echo commands entered by the user, and exit when the user types the command bye. Likewise, I created two private methods: printGreeting and printMessage for a cleaner code, and added Javadocs for them.
Level-2: Added the ability to store whatever text the user enters and display it back when requested.
Level-3: add mark/unmark commands and a Task class (A-Classes)
A-Coding standard: follow the seedu Java coding standard
Created three subclasses that extend Task class, and fixed Echo.java to show the correct output
A-CodeQuality: extract command dispatch out of main
commitResults.messageBody:
main() greets the user, runs the input loop, dispatches every command,
and prints the farewell. The dispatch chain sits at a lower level of
abstraction than the rest of main -- string slicing and Integer.parseInt
next to calls like printGreeting().

This breaks the Single Level of Abstraction Principle and makes main
harder to read as a summary of what the program does.

Let's move the if/else-if command chain into a private handleCommand
method. main() now reads as: greet, loop over input lines dispatching
each, then say goodbye. Behaviour is unchanged.
